title: LZO signature
summary: An LZO-compressed file does not have a standard magic number; LZO is typically used as a raw codec within containers (like LZO in PDF or SquashFS). The LZO1X format starts with a literal run.
source_version: Wikipedia List of file signatures, retrieved 2026-05-29

notes: LZO does not define a standard file format; it's a codec used within containers.
LZO1X is the most common variant.
LZO is used in SquashFS, PDF (DCTDecode is JPEG, not LZO), and Linux kernel (module compression).
